original_title: 10 Movies To Watch While Waiting for ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
summary_en: With Grand Theft Auto VI on the horizon, we've curated a list of films that capture the spirit of crime, chaos, and high-octane action you can expect.
ai_analysis: This list bridges the gap between gaming anticipation and cinematic escapism, offering viewers a taste of the GTA experience through film.

en.title: 7 Films to Fuel Your Hype for Grand Theft Auto VI
en.summary: With Grand Theft Auto VI on the horizon, we've curated a list of films that capture the spirit of crime, chaos, and high-octane action you can expect.
en.body:
## 1. 2 Fast 2 Furious
This high-octane sequel perfectly embodies the over-the-top car chases and vibrant, sun-drenched aesthetic that often defines the GTA universe. It's pure, unadulterated street racing mayhem with a focus on flashy vehicles and quick getaways, making it essential viewing for anyone craving that specific brand of vehicular adrenaline.

## 2. Tango & Cash
For a dose of classic buddy-cop action with a gritty, urban backdrop, look no further than this 1989 film. Sylvester Stallone and Kurt Russell’s chemistry fuels a story of wrongfully accused cops out for revenge, mirroring the kind of anti-heroic narratives GTA often explores. The film's blend of humor and hard-boiled action feels right at home with the series' tone.

## 3. Road House (2024 Remake)
Jake Gyllenhaal's turn as a bouncer in this reboot brings a raw, physical intensity that resonates with the often brutal world of open-world crime games. While the original is a cult classic, the remake injects a fresh, modern sensibility into its tales of bar brawls and protecting a community, offering a different flavor of close-quarters combat.

## 4. Red Dead Redemption 2
While technically a game, its inclusion here is a testament to its cinematic scope and narrative depth, developed by Rockstar Games themselves. Its sprawling open world, morally complex characters, and stunningly realized Wild West setting provide a masterclass in immersive storytelling that GTA VI is sure to build upon. The sheer detail in its world-building is unparalleled.

## 5. Cyberpunk 2077
This game plunges players into a neon-drenched, dystopian metropolis teeming with cybernetic enhancements and corporate intrigue. Its themes of identity, technology gone awry, and navigating a morally ambiguous future are strikingly similar to the kind of advanced urban environments GTA often envisions. The game's visual flair and narrative choices offer a glimpse into a potential GTA VI setting.

## 6. The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Though a departure in genre, this Nintendo masterpiece offers an unparalleled sense of freedom and emergent gameplay within a vast, explorable world. The sheer creativity and player agency it provides, allowing for unique solutions to challenges, echoes the sandbox potential players hope for in GTA VI. Its expansive Hyrule is a testament to player-driven adventure.

## 7. Into the Blue
This underwater crime thriller offers a change of pace with its exotic island setting and treasure-hunting plot, featuring Paul Walker and Jessica Alba. It captures a sense of adventure and the thrill of finding something valuable (or dangerous) beneath the waves, a different kind of heist that can appeal to the exploratory spirit GTA often ignites. The clear turquoise waters hide darker secrets.
Bottom Line: Get ready for Grand Theft Auto VI by diving into these films and games that share its DNA of action, freedom, and unforgettable worlds.

content_raw: So long as there’s no unforeseen disaster that occurs at some point within the next few weeks, Grand Theft Auto VI should finally come out, and at the time of writing, it’s about a month away. A new Grand Theft Auto game is always a big deal, especially since Grand Theft Auto IV was a full-on gaming blockbuster in 2008, and then 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V was even bigger, and it impressively came out within the same console generation as IV.
